title: Activity-aware warm pools and credit smoothing for Dedicated capacity
creator: Lena Park
description: This PRD defines a system to keep tenant capacity 'warm' based on recent activity signals and to smooth consumption credits over short bursts. The goal is to reduce cold-start latency for ephemeral workloads while bounding cost exposure from unbounded prewarming. Focus areas are warming heuristics, credit banking/smoothing, visibility in Console, and conservative billing rules for warm pool usage.
goals: Reduce 95th-percentile cold-start latency for Dedicated tenants by 40% for traffic spikes under 5 minutes
Introduce a tenant-level warm-credit ledger that smooths short bursts and prevents one-off spikes from consuming long-term reserved capacity unexpectedly
Expose warming state, credit balance, and predicted burn rate in Redwood Console for operator transparency
Provide safe default policies and an opt-in advanced mode for tenants to tune warming aggressiveness
non_goals: Replace existing reserved pool allocation and hard isolation guarantees
Support cross-tenant credit sharing in this phase (may be considered later)
Full integration with on-prem Private runtime billing in phase 1
user_stories: As an engineering lead for a SaaS tenant I want short-lived traffic spikes to use warm credits instead of failing or falling back to lower-quality models
As an operator I want to see each tenant's warm-credit balance and warming history so I can audit cost and troubleshoot regressions
As a platform engineer I want default safe thresholds so that warm pooling cannot be abused to bypass reserved capacity constraints
requirements: Telemetry: emit a per-tenant warming state event with timestamp, warm-slot count, predicted evaporation rate, and credit delta
Ledger: maintain a time-decayed credit balance per tenant with configurable half-life (default 1 hour)
Heuristics: warming decisions driven by recent RPS trends, tail-latency triggers, and user-configurable minimum idle retention
APIs: REST endpoint to query and adjust warm-credit policy per tenant and Console integration to surface policy and usage
Fallback: when warm credits exhausted, platform must fall back to normal burst policies with user-visible reason codes
Billing: warm-credit consumption must be distinguishable in billing exports and cost attribution reports
Safety: soft cap per tenant for warm-slots equal to 20% of reserved pool baseline, configurable by account tier
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end demo: provision a dedicated tenant, simulate a 3-minute 5x RPS spike and show 95th-pctl cold-start latency reduced >=40% compared to baseline without warming

Ledger correctness: for three synthetic burst scenarios (single short burst, two bursts within half-life, long sustained burst), credit balance evolves as documented in the spec and never goes negative
Console UX: warm-credit balance and policy are visible in tenant Cost & Capacity panel with a tooltip explaining credit decay and refill rules
Telemetry: warming-state events are ingested into the observability pipeline and visible in debug dashboards within 2 minutes
Billing export: warm-credit usage appears as a separate line item in the CSV export and maps to tenant ID
Safety enforcement: automated tests validate soft cap enforcement and a manual QA run verifies that warm-slots do not exceed the configured percentage across 100 tenants
success_metrics: 95th-percentile cold-start latency for warmed bursts decreases by >=40% for targeted tenants
Number of incidents attributed to cold-starts during short spikes decreases by 60% within first 60 days
Warm-credit related billing disputes under 0.5% of total Dedicated invoices after rollout
Adoption: >=30% of newly onboarded Dedicated tenants enable the default warm-credit policy within first month
implementation_notes: Runtime: augment the serving runtime to support prewarmed slot pinning with a soft expiration hook; avoid hard eviction until decay triggers
Orchestration: heuristics service runs asynchronously and posts warming commands to the capacity controller; controller enforces soft caps
Data model: ledger stored in Redis cluster with periodic durable snapshots to primary store for billing reconciliation
Console: add 'Warmth' card under Capacity tab and a pod-level indicator in route traces
Rollout plan: start with canary tenants (internal + 10 customers), monitor costs and SLOs for 3 weeks, then opt-in beta, followed by default-on gradual rollout
Privacy/Security: ledger entries include tenant ID only; no customer payloads are included
comments: 2025-02-13: Initial scoping session notes added. Trade-off discussed: aggressive prewarm reduces latency but increases short-term GPU ops and cost. Action: model predicted RPS rather than rely solely on instantaneous spikes. - Lena
2025-02-19: Eng review: Diego: prefer decoupled ledger service to avoid runtime GC pressure. Proposed Redis-backed ledger with TTLs. Assigned ENG-30121 to spike implementation.
2025-02-25: Design feedback: Priya Singh suggested Console visual affordances to avoid operator confusion between reserved capacity and warm credits. Will prototype two alternative cards. - Lena
2025-03-01: Security review kickoff: Security indicated encryption-at-rest for ledger snapshots required for enterprise tenants. Added to implementation notes. - Diego
2025-03-03: PM decision: default half-life set to 1 hour, soft cap 20%. Advanced mode exposed under Account Settings. Proceed to canary. - Lena
